prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1425; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a side impact at an intersection involving our insured vehicle. The claimant is represented by counsel, so all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and statements from two witnesses, who both describe the collision as occurring just as the claimant reported it. The other driver also confirms the sequence of events, and the claimant's account has matched across every conversation so far.

Entry 3: Photos of the vehicle show damage consistent with the described impact angle and force. A few older scratches are visible, though they may predate this crash and are being noted separately.

Entry 4: Confirmed through the police record and witness accounts that the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. The driver is listed by name on the policy, and nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before coverage began.

Entry 5: The reported whiplash is a plausible injury for a collision of this type. Medical records show no prior injury to the same area of the body. Treatment followed a typical course and tapered off as the claimant improved.

Entry 6: Reviewed the full file with the claim supervisor. Liability and vehicle damage align with the reported facts, and the injury claim is proceeding through standard evaluation with counsel.
